attribution.changes: Each mitigation is classified with one subcategory of the draft taxonomy, which was released for comment. The mitigation text is written for this prototype.

attribution.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act) and Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation), Official Journal of the European Union.
attribution.changes: Article numbers and titles are quoted; the mitigation text is written for this prototype. Only the text published in the Official Journal is authentic.

r2.description: Re-weight the flagged cohort, re-run the four-fifths test across all five protected attributes, and hold the scale decision until every cohort is within tolerance.
r2.why: A.5 owns assessing impacts on groups, and the disparity test that flagged the cohort is filed under it.

r2.description: Examine bureau and account-behaviour features for proxies of protected traits, and drop or constrain the ones that act as proxies.
r2.why: Proxies enter through the training data, whose provenance and preparation A.7 governs.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 10: Data and data governance

r3.description: Compare the score distribution and approval rates with the calibration baseline every month, and trigger a recalibration review when they move past a set threshold.
r3.why: Monitoring between reviews is part of running the model through its life cycle, which A.6 owns.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 72: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan for high-risk AI systems

r3.description: Re-validate the model after every change in the bank base rate, not only at the quarterly review.
r3.why: A rate change is the drift trigger the risk names, and re-validation is a life-cycle step under A.6.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 15: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity

s-rcr-3.description: Build each decline's reason codes from that applicant's own score contributions, and test a sample of declines to check the stated reasons match what drove the score.
s-rcr-3.why: Reason codes are the information an applicant is given, which A.8 covers.

sources.title: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 22: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 86: Right to explanation of individual decision-making

s-rcr-4.description: Ask underwriters to record their own reason when they confirm a decline, and sample confirmed declines each month for the depth of review.
s-rcr-4.why: A.9 owns how the system is used, including the human oversight of each decline.

sources.title: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 22: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 14: Human oversight

s-rcr-4.description: Name underwriting in the role charter as accountable for every decline, with the authority and time to overturn the score.
s-rcr-4.why: Who holds the decision and the authority to overrule the model is a matter of roles, which A.3 sets.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems

s-rcr-5.description: Report accuracy separately for thin-file, young and recently moved applicants, and send low-confidence thin-file scores to manual underwriting instead of an automatic decline.
s-rcr-5.why: Unequal accuracy across groups is an impact on those groups, which A.5 assesses.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 10: Data and data governance

r5.description: Hold back any answer for which the groundedness check finds no supporting passage, and show the agent the cited source beside every answer.
r5.why: The guardrail sits where agents use the system, which A.9 governs.

r5.description: Track the citation-support rate weekly on sampled answers, and re-open the impact assessment if it falls below the pilot baseline.
r5.why: Ongoing evaluation after release is a life-cycle duty under A.6.

r9.description: Treat customer text as data, not instructions: keep it apart from the system prompt, filter known injection patterns, and limit what the assistant can retrieve in that session.
r9.why: Input handling is designed into the system, which is life-cycle work under A.6.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 15: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity

r9.description: Run an injection test suite before each release, and log suspected injections for incident review.
r9.why: Release testing is a life-cycle gate under A.6.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 15: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity

s-chatbot-3.description: Remove withdrawn and replaced documents from the index on the day they change, and check each night that every indexed policy is the current version.
s-chatbot-3.why: The index is the data the copilot answers from, and its currency is a data-quality matter for A.7.

s-chatbot-4.description: Filter retrieval by the agent's business-unit permissions, so documents and their titles from other units never reach the prompt or the answer.
s-chatbot-4.why: Which documents may feed an answer is a question of data access, which A.7 governs.

sources.title: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 25: Data protection by design and by default
GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 32: Security of processing

s-chatbot-5.description: Ask agents to open the cited source before sending an answer about fees, terms or eligibility, and sample sent answers for unchecked use.
s-chatbot-5.why: A.9 owns how agents use the system and keep human oversight over it.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 14: Human oversight

s-chatbot-5.description: State in the AI use policy that a copilot answer is a draft the agent remains accountable for.
s-chatbot-5.why: Rules for staff use of AI belong in the AI policy set, which A.2 holds.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems

s-chatbot-6.description: State in the AI use policy that customers' account and personal details are never pasted into the copilot, and enforce it with a redaction filter in front of the model.
s-chatbot-6.why: What staff may put into an AI tool is an AI policy rule, which A.2 holds.

sources.title: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 5: Principles relating to processing of personal data
GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 25: Data protection by design and by default

s-chatbot-6.description: Agree zero retention of prompts with the model provider, and check it in the provider's supplier assessment.
s-chatbot-6.why: Retention at the provider is a supplier commitment, which A.10's third-party controls cover.

sources.title: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 5: Principles relating to processing of personal data
GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 32: Security of processing

r1.description: Keep the use case held at the gate until the fundamental-rights impact assessment is signed off, completed with the affected groups and the bias-audit results.
r1.why: The FRIA is an impact assessment, which A.5 owns, and the board made it a gate condition.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 27: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems

r4.description: Commission an independent bias audit of the ranking before any shortlist is produced, and repeat it for each new model version.
r4.why: Auditing before release is a life-cycle step under A.6, where the risk is recorded.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 10: Data and data governance

r4.description: Make a passed bias audit a release condition in the model's life-cycle checklist.
r4.why: Release conditions are part of the life cycle that A.6 governs.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 9: Risk management system

s-hiring-3.description: Keep past recruiter shortlists out of retraining until they are audited for bias, and compare each new version's shortlist rates by group before release.
s-hiring-3.why: Which past decisions become training data is a data-preparation choice under A.7.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 10: Data and data governance

s-hiring-4.description: Give each rejected candidate the main factors behind their ranking and a way to ask for a human review.
s-hiring-4.why: What candidates are told is information for interested parties, which A.8 covers.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 86: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 22: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling

s-hiring-5.description: Strip special-category data and its clear proxies from CV text before scoring, and record the lawful basis for anything that remains in the data protection impact assessment.
s-hiring-5.why: Preparing the CV data before it is scored is data work under A.7.

sources.title: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 9: Processing of special categories of personal data
GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 35: Data protection impact assessment

s-hiring-6.description: Make documentation of the vendor model's training data and design a contract condition before the pilot, and audit the model against it.
s-hiring-6.why: The duty sits with the vendor, so it is secured through the third-party controls of A.10.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 13: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems

s-hiring-7.description: Name the recruiter accountable for each shortlist in the hiring role charter, and require them to review every rejection below the cut-off.
s-hiring-7.why: Accountability for each shortlist is a role assignment, which A.3 sets.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 14: Human oversight
EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems

s-hiring-7.description: Limit how many applications each recruiter reviews a day, and sample rejected applications for candidates the ranking missed.
s-hiring-7.why: A.9 owns how recruiters use the ranking and keep oversight of it.

sources.title: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 14: Human oversight
